items.title: Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says
items.description: Pope Leo had successful surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican said.

items.title: Saudi man charged with planting 'sophisticated' recording device in OpenAI office
items.description: Prosecutors say the device, wrapped in toilet paper, was found inserted in a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room.

items.title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI
items.description: Sir Ken McCallum says operations to tackle terrorism and state threats are now roughly of an "equal scale".

items.title: Missiles intercepted near Riyadh after Saudi coalition hits Yemen fuel depot
items.description: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen struck a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa.

items.title: Ex-gang boss sentenced to 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
items.description: Davis was found guilty last month over his role in the late rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in 1996.

items.title: Cornell bans all fraternity parties over gang sex assault allegations
items.description: The school has faced an uproar over how it handled assault allegations brought by a woman known as Jane Doe.

items.title: Trump ousts Kimberly Guilfoyle as US ambassador to Greece after corruption allegations
items.description: Guilfoyle said the allegations of improper conduct were false and that being ambassador was the "honour of a lifetime".

items.title: Horrified witnesses recount fatal rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
items.description: Police say preliminary information suggests the man who died at the Georgia amusement park fell from a ride.

items.title: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
items.description: In his first interview since being forced from his post, Gen Syrskyi speaks about Ukraine's future in the war.

items.title: Argentina targets UK in legal claim over Falklands oil exploration
items.description: The action filed with an international maritime tribunal is the latest development in an escalating row over the Falkland Islands.

items.title: Watch: Emergency calls from botched Christa Pike execution released
items.description: A series of calls, obtained by the Associated Press, reveal emergency services were delayed in reaching Pike.

items.title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
items.description: Mitte, who lived with cerebral palsy, starred as Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series.

items.title: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack
items.description: Six crew members are rescued but 10 are missing after a merchant ship was sunk overnight, Bulgaria says.

items.title: BBC FM radio transmissions suspended in Afghanistan
items.description: BBC programming is still reaching audiences on shortwave, medium wave, via satellite and online.

items.title: 'I'd talk to the TV': The paid companions bringing warmth to China's lonely
items.description: As loneliness grows in China, a new industry is emerging to provide companionship and support.

items.title: Who's to blame for the toxic smog choking South East Asia?
items.description: Anger is mounting at the companies accused of burning land in Indonesia and the authorities who have failed to stop them.

items.title: Pakistan has locked down Imran Khan's stronghold - but it could backfire
items.description: Some fear the government's standoff with the former PM's supporters could bring more instability, not less.

items.title: Is Zelensky right to say data centre strikes have taken down Russian bots?
items.description: Experts say there is no evidence that Russian trolls have been affected by Ukraine’s Yandex attacks.

items.title: The island where locals say data centres are taking their water
items.description: "Not a single drop has come through our taps for the last three months," a local tells the BBC.

items.title: Why the lonely in China are hiring 'temporary children'
items.description: A new industry being dubbed the “loneliness economy” has emerged in China, with people hiring themselves out as companions to help the elderly.
